newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Maxim starting trials - CEO.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Maxim starting trials - CEO.

text.p: Maxim Pharmaceuticals Inc will be starting Phase III trials of its Maxamine cancer therapy any day, chief executive Larry Stambaugh told Reuters.
If all goes as expected, he said, marketing of the drug in the United States should begin in mid-1999.

Stating the start of the Phase III trials should trigger Maxim's share price. Alfred Berg last week initiated coverage of the stock with a buy rating saying, "Our 12-month target for Maxim share is on the upper side of $25."
The stock closed Monday at 9, up 3/8.

"Judging from the current evaluation," the firm wrote, investors seem to have completely overlooked the significance of Swedish clinical test Phase IIb data for (Maxim's) Maxamine fatal skin and leukemia treatment."
It pointed out the company has also been given a go-ahead signal for a limited hepatitis C trial with Maxamine in Sweden, where the drug was discovered.
Given the over 45 million people worldwide "infected with Hepatitis C, we believe that Maxim would become a takeover target, should the Hepatitis C trials become a success," Alfred Berg said.

The firm projects Maxim's initial revenues will come in fiscal 1999, ending September 30, totaling $16 million for the year. It further sees revenues of $67 million in fiscal 2000 when the company will have its first profit, $12 million pretax at a rate of 10 percent for earnings per share of $1.
Asked about Alfred Berg's expectation the company will "reach an after-tax profit of close to $60 million five years from now," Stambaugh said "That's pretty do-able."
Chief Financial Officer Dale Sander said the development stage company's burn rate will be about $7 million this year and is now slated for $8 million in fiscal 1998.
The company "may decide to increase (the spending rate) in the coming year" he said, adding it could be as high as $10 or $11 million.

This net level of spending makes no provision for funds the company may get from new partners or sale of more stock, Sander said, noting the company is now discussing an equity sale with investment bankers.

Stambaugh said Maxim is telling pharmaceutical companies seeking to market its drugs once they receive approval they will have to provide up front funding while tests are underway. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212 859-1610))
